content:
A page per declaration: what it says, what it uses, and what uses it. That last one is what I could not get anywhere else.

Mathlib: https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/
Navier-Stokes: https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/?p=nse
FLT: https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/?p=flt

FLT is the interesting one. It is unfinished, so every theorem still resting on 'sorry' is flagged, and you can see how much stands on each hole.

It reads .olean files with Tenet, my Lean 4 kernel in C#, so nothing runs Lean and Mathlib takes two minutes.

MIT.

Nice!
(I wanted to look at Navier-Stokes but it seems to be missing.)

Bjørn Kjos-Hanssen said:

Nice!
(I wanted to look at Navier-Stokes but it seems to be missing.)

It's there now sorry had to get the CI correct.

This is slick. Its probably really computationally expensive, but it would be cool to have it be able to walk an arbitrarily specified public github repo in real time. You could even mimic the loading graphics from WinDirStat.

It seems like you don't actually give the full terms for definitions, only the type signature. e.g.
https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/?p=flt#/d/LinearEquiv.symm

I feel like it would be better if you full showed how defs are defined.

@Colin Bundschu Both are in. Paste any public GitHub repo, it clones, builds, re-checks every proof and shows as a library. Did lean4-cli and batteries today.

Real time I can't do. The cost is 'lake build', not the drawing. Ten minutes for small, hours for big. The loading graphic at least tells you which step it's on.

@Jack McCarthy You're right, it was never wired up. The body is right there in the .olean, the printer just only ever got the type.

Defs carry their body now. 223,300 in Mathlib, 56 MB, averaging 261 chars.

Downside: it's the elaborated term not your source. Structure instances come back as let __src✝ := ... and the source link is still there for what you typed. Defs only, no theorems. Proof terms average 22k chars and some blow past 400k.

@Jack McCarthy follow-up: the source is in the page now too, right under the term. So you get both, what the kernel checked and what you actually typed.

https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/?p=mathlib#/d/Function.comp

Not new info, just easier to look at. I put con-leche into LeanViz so you can click through it:
https://keithadler.github.io/leanviz/?p=conleche#/d/ConLeche.model_exists

@Sam Tobin-Hochstadt on your porting question, this might help size it up. 'model_exists' leans on 25,005 things. About 17,700 of those are con-leche's own work, the other 7,300 come from core. So the bulk of it is Joachim's, not inherited.

Both big theorems only use the three standard axioms, and nothing rests on 'sorry'.

You could get all this from Lean in a few minutes. It's just nice to be able to hover and click.
Can one have a local version of this, in case of wanting to look at a project that's not able to be public (yet)?

Hi @Keith Adler,
The site is currently broken for me. When I go to any of the links above I am unable to click on anything. There is only a search bar.
@Jack McCarthy Fix releasing adding tests on the UI side thanks.
